aft_wall_is_connector_panel: 3 x PG11 glands, power button, charge port - all panel-mount through the module aft wall, all inside the service strip
blocker_installed_at: STEP 7, from BELOW, before the plate goes on - its spigot has to go up into the foam's bore and its body fills the plate's. Leads pull up through the slit at step 18 and only the BUNG grips them
blocker_is: printed ASA, O30.4 x 4 inside the PLATE's bore with a O23.6 x 12 spigot up into the foam's, bedded on 4200. A 22 x 7 SLIT for the leads - clearance, not a seal. Nothing is machined into the alu: the dense block is simply bored NARROWER, and the foam ring that leaves is the stop
blocker_load_path: the 4200 bond on the spigot, NOT the foam ring. The ring is 293 mm2 at 2.17 MPa against H80's 1.4, so it would crush in on its own; the bond is 890 mm2 in shear at 2.8x. If the bond is skimped the ring is what is left
bung_compressed_by: the GONG MAST'S HEAD, drawn up face to face with the board's bottom by the four M6s at step 23. NOT the board's own hardpoint plate - that is bonded in at step 7 and never moves
bung_follower_would_fix: a rigid disc between the bung and the mast plate, sized to the bore, spanning the slot - the follower out of any stuffing box. It is the only thing that gets the plate's push onto the whole bung face, and it also decouples the squeeze from the rubber's stock thickness, which is the other thing biting here
bung_installs_from: BELOW, up the plate's own bore, leads already threaded. Nothing is machined for it and nothing compresses it - the plate is bonded in at step 7 and cannot move at step 18
bung_land_settled_by: MEASURED: Derek's slot is 20.4 x 7, cut just wide enough for the three leads side by side. It sits wholly under the bung, so it costs only its own 143 mm2 - the mast plate keeps 89% of the bung's face. No follower, no flange, no spotface
bung_layout: three in a row along the chord
bung_note: O30.0 x 12.700 punched from 3/4 in 50A neoprene, three 5.5 mm holes in a row at 7.5 pitch. Fills the plate's ONE STRAIGHT O30.8 bore top to bottom, butts the epoxy liner's end face, and hangs 4.000 mm below the wetted face. The GONG MAST'S PLATE squeezes that out - 31% - as the four M6 bolts pull it face to face with the board.
bung_plate_machining: ONE STRAIGHT O30.8 BORE, no step and no counterbore - the stop is the epoxy liner's end face where the foam channel steps down to O22, which is there anyway
bung_relief_path: extrudes down into the mast plate's wire slot and up the conduit - both open, so the squeeze cannot lock solid
bung_seal_ranked: 1. the O5.5 holes at 15% on the leads - a grommet seal, and it does not need the squeeze at all. 2. the bung's OD closing onto the bore, which takes only 17% of the displaced volume so it arrives whatever else happens. 3. the axial squeeze, of which 5% of the face has somewhere to escape to - treat it as help, not as the mechanism. 4. the 4200 fillet over the lot
cell_holder_pitch_source: V1 measured, Heyiarbeit brackets - model and bought part agree
cell_holders: bought 1x2 spacer bricks, THROUGH-HOLE, top and bottom of every cell - they locate the cells and set the pitch, and add no height
charge_port: SP17 2-pin flange socket, threaded coupling with a SCREW CAP - chosen over the EW-LP16's nicer one-touch latch because the LP16's cover is a press-fit bung, and this is the lowest unrated opening into the module and it is unmated every ride
conduit_route: TWO STRAIGHT BORES. One straight up from the mast plate, 32 mm of it. One drilled down from inside the cavity at 48 deg, 43 mm of it. They meet in the foam at z=30, above the blocker
conduit_why_straight: this channel is cut BY HAND at step 18 into a board assembled since step 7. No drill makes a swept radius through a bonded-in foam block from either end, so the curve the model used to draw was not a buildable part. Two straight bores meeting in the foam are
deck_pad: THREE pieces - aft of the hatch, forward of it, and one on the lid. No seams within a piece, all corners radiused, edge held to the deck slope so it stays on top

glass_edges.lid recess wall to ring top: concave - thickened epoxy fillet at layup
glass_edges.rebate wall to rim ledge: SQUARE - ring seat, glassed in, not a laminate path
glass_edges.rim ring outer face: flush with the recess wall - no corner

handle_mount: bought kayak grab handle on 2 x M6 at 153 mm centres, TAPPED into a 12.7 mm 6061 strip set TANGENT to the rail under the skin - NO recess, so the 38 mm the handle stands proud at mid-span is the whole finger clearance
handles: 2 x surface-mounted rail handle, port and starboard beside the hatch, + 1 on the module - one bought part in all three places
hardpoint_material: H-80 dense PVC - 1/2 and 3/4 in are H-80 only. Leash plug bond is 1.4x, the thinnest margin on the board.
hatch_alignment: CNC cuts all 12 bosses AND all 12 bolt holes in one setup, so the pattern is mutually accurate and the lid aligns as one rigid body. The O16 resin boss is the recovery path for a stray hole, not the primary method - re-pot and re-drill that one on a transfer mark
hatch_buried_washer_note: FITS, at O17.0 - the most the 10.5 mm edge distance allows - landing at 1.19 MPa against the core's 2.0. But it spreads into FOAM, it is buried at layup so a bad hole cannot be recovered, and it cannot be countersunk: the cone wants 0.0 mm of solid material and the skin over it is 1.2
hatch_fastening: M5 through the lid into a CAPTIVE M5 NUT printed into the ASA ring. PRINT SEAL FACE DOWN - the bed gives a flatter, smoother seal land than any top surface will, and the 4 x 2.4 groove then only has to bridge 4 mm, which ASA does without support. Pause at print Z = 4.5 mm, drop 12 M5 nuts into their pockets, resume. Steel thread, so the hatch can come off every ride for ever without wearing anything
hatch_head_style: M5 button head, ISO 7380 - domed, 2.75 tall
hatch_seal: O3 silicone cord BONDED into a 4 x 2.4 groove, 20% squeeze, hard stop
hatch_seat_is: a O16 epoxy plug poured through the BARE CORE at every bolt, before the skins go on, plus a O18 penny washer under the head
hatch_seat_load_is: the applied preload, not the seal demand
hatch_washer_vs_boss: a O18 penny washer now passes at 1.78x on FOAM, where the potted boss runs 1.9x on EPOXY and never loads the core at all. Foam past 2.0 MPa sets permanently and a hard-stop joint then seals at the wrong squeeze; epoxy at 24 MPa does not move. The boss also keeps the heads flush, which the washer cannot
joint: no floor groove - aluminium floor; shell prints in 4 L-shaped pieces split at wall midpoints, paired 10 mm proud x 24 external ribs, dovetailed and acetone-welded at each seam, + 6 mm glass-tape fillet inside every corner
leash_plug: FCS pattern, O30.2 x 12.7 deep bore in a 70 mm H200 pad, milled flat
leash_plug_part: bought cup, O30 x 12.5 deep, stainless pin - 0.16 mm of bond gap on the diameter
mach_wall_finish_bit: 1/2 in spiral, 76.2 mm of flute, against a 71.6 mm wall - in the BOM. Rough with the Freud
mach_workholding: tape or vacuum to the spoilboard, every setup - each one presents a flat face
mast_bolt_governed_by: the M6 BOLT's proof load - Gong's own screw, and now the weak link. The 6061 thread is 46% stronger than it and there is nothing to be gained by tapping deeper
mast_bolt_is: M6 x 30, T30 TORX, supplied by Gong - 7 of them come in the setup with 4 brass square nuts and 4 cup washers. NOT M8: this model said M8 until it was checked against Gong's own contents list
mast_fastening: M6 TAPPED 10 mm blind into a 12.7 mm 6061-T651 plate from the pad face - 2.7 mm of solid alu above. No bushings, no bonding, no lathe. Tef-Gel every bolt: alu + A4 in a wet cavity
mast_head_t_derived_from: Gong's M6x30 through it must leave 10 mm in the tap
mast_margin_note: 1.44x is against the M6's PROOF load, not its ultimate - about 2.0x against failure. It is Gong's screw into our tapped 6061, and our side is 46% stronger than the screw, so nothing we build moves it. A US-rail board reacts the same screw into a brass square nut in a plastic box, which is weaker than this
mast_plate_thickness_set_by: the THREAD, not the footprint: M6 tapped 10 blind with 2.7 mm of solid alu left above it
mast_why_machined: blind tapped, so no clearance absorbs error: true position must hold 0.25 mm, a 2 deg drill wander alone spends 0.35 mm of it, and only 2.7 mm of solid alu separates the tap from breaching the plate that keeps the cavity dry

materials.cell holder: bought 21700 1x2 spacer bricks, both ends of every cell - NOT the printed comb below, which is dead code
materials.hatch lid: glass 1.2 / H100 (2 x 1/4in bonded - no 1/2in H100 exists) PVC foam 13 / glass 1.2 = 15.2 mm
materials.hatch rim ring: PRINTED ASA, 12.7 mm, 6 pieces (acetone weld, dovetailed), no joint on a corner, bedded in 4200 and glassed in
materials.hatch seal: O3 silicone cord BONDED into a 4 x 2.4 groove PRINTED INTO the ring - depth is layer count, not a router pass
materials.hull core: EPS ~2 lb/ft3, CNC milled in two halves, seam at 1030 mm
materials.hull skin: E-glass 2 x 6 oz + 1708 biax, vacuum bagged
materials.mast hardpoint block: Divinycell H80 dense PVC foam - full depth to the deck aft of the cavity, 30 mm slab under it, 6061 plate let into its underside
materials.mast plate: 6061-T651 aluminium, 12.7 mm, M6 tapped 10 blind - no bushings
materials.module flange rail: printed integral with the wall, 20 x 14.5 mm
materials.module lid: glass 1.0 / H80 PVC foam 6 / glass 1.0 = 8.3 mm
materials.module shell: PRINTED ASA, 4 mm walls, 4 L-pieces split at wall midpoints / 3.2 mm 5052 aluminium floor, no divider

module_flange: OUTWARD 11 mm, 14.5 thick - 15 mm of land, band on the wall top
module_floor_joint: ASA wall bonded to the 5052 floor on a 2 mm controlled bond line, filleted BOTH sides - inside, and outside onto the 3 mm ledge the floor is oversized by. Structural POLYURETHANE, not epoxy: the two materials differ by 66 um/m/K, which is 0.60 mm from the centre over 40 C, and a rigid bond line would see 299% shear strain
module_handle_load_is: SHEAR, not pull-out - a single-hole strap end pins and rotates until its line of action goes through the bolt, so there is no prying moment for a second bolt to resist
module_handle_redundancy: 2 fasteners carry the whole module. Loctite both, and they are on the pre-ride list
module_lift_handle: 2 printed pads on the AFT wall at y +/-35, 12 mm proud, 1 x M5 heat-set each on the pad centreline - the strap end has one hole, so the pedestal pins and the bolt works in SHEAR. One pad per print piece, so only the handle crosses the seam. Aft because the module butts the forward cavity wall - this is the only reachable face
module_seal: closed-cell sponge EPDM, 3 mm uncompressed -> 2.0 at 33% squeeze. FULL FACE, one piece over the whole 15 mm land, punched for the bolts - V1's method
module_vent: M12 Gore-type membrane vent THROUGH the AFT wall, between the handle's far pad and the conduit - IP68 to water, open to gas both ways. Axis along X, like every other fitting in that wall
motor_mount: saddle clamp on the mast trailing edge
ring_face_machining: groove PRINTED 1.8 deep, plugged with a sacrificial filler, glassed over with the rest of the deck, then opened with a 2.5 mm cutter through ~0.6 of glass into the filler. Finished depth 2.4 = glass land to printed floor. Laminate stays CONTINUOUS and the land is glass, not ASA
service_bay_holds: mast conduit gland, 3 x PG11 module glands, power button, charge port
vent_flood_note: the module breathes into the CAVITY. A flooded cavity submerges the membrane, and IP68 is an immersion rating not a permanent head. The cavity can hold this much water before the vent becomes the module's weak point - and the leak alarm's sensor sits on the module floor, so it should find it long before that
